title: Real conversations
goal: Handle problems, give opinions, link your sentences, and get through a phone call and a home visit.

notes.p: Korean describes most problems in the past tense, because the thing has already happened: {{잃어버렸어요}} (I lost it), {{고장 났어요}} (it broke, so it's broken now), {{길을 잃었어요}} (I lost the way, so I'm lost). {{도와주세요}} = please help me. Sound point: in {{무슨 일}} an extra ㄴ sound appears before {{일}}, so it is said {{무슨 닐}}.

Take the polite form, drop the final {{요}}, and add {{야 돼요}}: {{가요}} becomes {{가야 돼요}}, {{벗어요}} becomes {{벗어야 돼요}}, {{해요}} becomes {{해야 돼요}}. Ask it as a question for "do I have to?" or "do I need to?".
ex: I have to get up early tomorrow.
Do I have to take off my shoes?

notes.p: {{-지만}} is a plain "but": {{비싸지만 맛있어요}}. {{-는데}} sets the scene before a question or a request and makes it softer: {{길을 잃었는데 좀 도와주실 수 있어요?}} = I'm lost; could you help me? Action words, {{있어요}} words and the past take {{는데}} ({{있는데}}, {{잃었는데}}). Describing words take {{은데}} or just {{ㄴ데}} ({{좋은데}}, {{바쁜데}}). Ending a sentence with {{-는데요}} trails off politely: {{지금 좀 바쁜데요}}.
ex: 길을 잃었는데 좀 도와주실 수 있어요?
I'm lost. Could you help me?
I'm a bit busy right now...

notes.p: {{그래서}} = so, that's why. {{그런데}} = but, or by the way. {{그러면}} = then, in that case. While you listen, react: {{아, 그래요?}} (oh, really?), {{그렇군요}} (I see), {{그렇죠}} (right, exactly), {{맞아요}} (that's right).
ex: The bus didn't come. That's why I was late.
It's delicious. But it's a bit expensive.
Are you busy today? Then let's meet tomorrow.

notes.p: {{것 같아요}} = I think, it seems. The word in front shows the time: {{비가 오는 것 같아요}} (I think it's raining), {{비가 올 것 같아요}} (I think it's going to rain). Describing words use their noun form: {{좋은 것 같아요}} (I think it's good), {{맛있는 것 같아요}} (I think it's tasty). {{생각해요}} = I think: {{저도 그렇게 생각해요}}. Sound point: {{같아요}} after {{것}} starts tight, {{까타요}}, and after {{올}} the {{것}} is tight too: {{올 것 같아요}} is said {{올 껃 까타요}}.
ex: I think it's going to rain.

vocab.note: Also what you shout in an emergency.
Polite, with {{-시-}} for the other person.
For machines: phones, the AC, an elevator.

items.en: I lost my wallet.
items.why: {{잃어버렸어요}} = I lost it. {{잊어버렸어요}}, with ㅈ, means I forgot.

items.en: The air conditioner is broken.
items.why: The fixed phrase is {{고장 났어요}}: it broke, so it's broken now.

items.en: This phone is broken.
items.why: The broken thing is the subject of {{고장 났어요}}: {{휴대폰이}}.

items.en: I have to get up early tomorrow.
items.why: Have to = {{-아야 돼요}}. {{일어나}} already ends in {{아}}, so it's just {{일어나야 돼요}}.

items.en: Do I have to take off my shoes?
items.why: {{벗어요}} becomes {{벗어야 돼요}}.

items.en: Korean is hard, but it's fun.
items.why: {{-지만}} = but. {{어려워서}} would mean "because it's hard".

items.q: 길을 잃었___ 좀 도와주실 수 있어요?
items.en: I'm lost. Could you help me?
items.why: {{-는데}} sets the scene before a request: {{잃었는데}}.

items.en: The weather is nice. Shall we go out together?
items.why: Describing words take {{은데}}: {{좋은데}}. {{-아서}} can't come before a suggestion like {{나갈까요?}}

items.en: Are you busy today? Then let's meet tomorrow.
items.why: {{그러면}} = then, in that case.

items.en: The bus didn't come. That's why I was late.
items.why: {{그래서}} = so, that's why.

items.en: It's delicious. But it's a bit expensive.
items.why: {{그런데}} = but.

items.en: I think it's going to rain.
items.why: For the future use {{올 것 같아요}}. {{오는 것 같아요}} = I think it's raining now; {{온 것 같아요}} = I think it rained.

items.en: I think this restaurant is good.
items.why: {{있어요}} words take {{는}}: {{맛있는 것 같아요}}.

items.en: I think so too.
items.why: {{그렇게 생각해요}} = I think so.

items.en: (On the phone) Hello? Who's calling?
items.why: {{여보세요}} is the phone hello.

items.en: Please sit and make yourself comfortable.
items.why: A polite request to a guest uses {{-으세요}}: {{앉으세요}}.

items.q: You arrive at Minji's home for dinner and hand her a small gift. You say:
items.why: {{초대해 주셔서 감사합니다}} = thank you for inviting me. {{들어오세요}} is what the host says.

items.q: Your guests are leaving your home late at night. You say:
items.why: They are leaving, so {{가세요}}: {{조심히 가세요}} = get home safely.

items.q: Your phone rings and you pick up. You say:
items.why: {{여보세요}} is only used on the phone.

items.q: You're lost in Seoul. You stop a stranger and politely ask for help:
opts: 저기요, 길을 잃었는데 좀 도와주실 수 있어요?
items.why: {{-는데}} sets up the request and {{도와주실 수 있어요?}} is polite. {{도와줘}} is casual speech, rude to a stranger.

items.q: Junho tells you {{저 다음 달에 결혼해요!}} You react:
items.why: {{진짜요?}} shows surprise and {{축하해요}} = congratulations. {{그래서요?}} sounds like "so what?"

items.q: You're stuck in traffic and will probably be late. You text your friend:
items.why: A guess about the future: {{늦을 것 같아요}} = I think I'll be late.

items.q: The air conditioner in your hotel room isn't working. You tell the front desk:
items.why: It's broken now: {{고장 났어요}}, with the broken thing as the subject ({{에어컨이}}).

items.q: Your friend says {{이 카페 정말 좋네요.}} You agree, and add that it's a bit expensive. You say:
items.why: {{그렇죠}} agrees, and {{그런데}} = but.

items.en: I lost my phone.
I have to go home now.
Korean is hard, but it's fun.
I think it's going to rain tomorrow.
What do you think of this?
Please come in. Make yourself comfortable.
The bus didn't come, so I was late.
Excuse me, could you take a photo for me?
items.full: 죄송한데 사진 좀 찍어 주실 수 있어요?

items.en: I don't feel well, so I'm going to rest at home.
items.full: 몸이 안 좋아서 집에서 쉴 거예요.

items.en: I'll call you again later.
Thank you for inviting me.
It's expensive, but I think it's good.

items.why: {{잃어버렸어요}} (lost) has an ㄹ sound; {{잊어버렸어요}} (forgot) has a j sound.

opts: It was expensive, but it was delicious.
I don't think I'll be late.
I think it's going to rain.
Hello? I can't hear you well.
Hello? I can hear you well.
Hello? I can't see you well.
So I didn't want to go.
I want it to be good.
items.why: {{좋을}} (future) ends in an l sound; {{좋은}} (now) ends in n.

opts: Do I have to take off my shoes?
Do I have to put on my shoes?
Can I take off my shoes?
Did you take off your shoes?
Do I have to buy shoes?

turns.why: It already happened, so past: {{잃어버렸어요}}. The phone is the object: {{휴대폰을}}.

turns.en: What does the phone look like?

turns.why: End the sentence with {{커요}}. {{큰}} only works right before a noun.
{{맞아요}} = that's right, then thank them. {{잘 먹었습니다}} is only for after a meal.
A guess about what will happen: {{늦을 것 같아요}}. {{같았어요}} would mean "I thought I'd be late".

turns.en: That's okay. How long will it take?

turns.why: Minutes use Sino-Korean numbers: {{삼십 분}}. You're still on the way, so a future guess: {{걸릴 것 같아요}}.

turns.en: Okay. Then I'll wait in the café.

turns.why: The guest thanks the host for the invitation. {{어서 오세요}} is the host's line.
Before you start eating: {{잘 먹겠습니다}}. {{잘 먹었습니다}} is for after the meal.
You're eating it now, so the present: {{맛있어요}}.

turns.en: Shall we go hiking together this weekend?

opts: 좋아요. 그런데 토요일에 비가 올 것 같아요.
좋아요. 그래서 토요일에 비가 올 것 같아요.
turns.why: {{그런데}} = but: sounds good, but it looks like rain on Saturday.

turns.en: Oh, really? Then shall we go on Sunday?

turns.why: {{좋은 생각이에요}} = that's a good idea: {{좋은}} before the noun {{생각}}.
You need to go there now: {{가야 돼요}}. {{가야 했어요}} is past (I had to go).
Subway lines use Sino-Korean numbers with {{호선}}: Line 2 is {{이 호선}}. {{이 시}} would be two o'clock.

roleplay.title: Lost phone at the station
roleplay.setup: You left your phone on the subway in Seoul. Go to the station office, explain the problem, and describe your phone.
roleplay.persona: You are a helpful member of staff at a Seoul subway station office. Three phones were handed in today: a black one, a white one, and a big blue one. Ask what happened, what the phone looks like (colour, size), and about what time and on which line they lost it. The learner's phone is the black one; once they describe it, give it back and ask them to write their name. Speak simple polite Korean (해요체 and -세요 forms) using mostly words from levels 1-10: 무슨 일이세요?, 어떤 휴대폰이에요?, 몇 시쯤?, 이거예요?, 다행이에요. Keep every sentence short.
goals: Explain that you lost your phone
Say roughly when you lost it

roleplay.title: Dinner at a friend's home
roleplay.setup: Your Korean friend Minji has invited you to dinner at her apartment. Arrive, eat, chat, and leave politely.
roleplay.persona: You are Minji, a warm Korean woman in her thirties hosting the learner for dinner at your apartment in Seoul. Welcome them in (어서 오세요, 들어오세요), point out the slippers, invite them to sit (편하게 앉으세요), serve bulgogi and japchae (많이 드세요), and ask their opinion of the food and of Seoul (어때요?, 어떻게 생각해요?). React naturally (아, 그래요?, 그렇군요, 그렇죠). When they leave, see them off with 조심히 가세요. Speak simple polite Korean (해요체) using mostly words from levels 1-10. Keep every sentence short.
goals: Ask whether to take off your shoes
Give your opinion of the food with "I think"
Say goodbye the right way when you leave
